messages:
alex: Quick async question — planning a small change to default model selection for /generate. Idea: add an optional request header `Accept-Model` that clients can send to pin a model version; if absent we keep the current default. Need to confirm compatibility constraints, error semantics, and a deprecation/comms plan.
emily: header > query param in my opinion. cleaner and easier for SDKs. agree it should be opt-in: missing header = current default. also we must surface the actual model used in the response envelope so clients can assert which model served the request.
zach: +1 to header. couple of concerns: 1) SDK ergonomics — expose an easy API for passing the header in js/python. 2) telemetry — we need counters for `accept_model` usage vs default. 3) param compatibility: some params (e.g., `nucleus`, specific sampling options) might not be supported by older model variants. how do we handle that?
dena: from product — we want a clear migration path and deprecation timeline. propose: feature flag for orgs to opt into header, then public opt-in via docs, then a 6-month migration window after we announce a non-default change, with 30/14/7 day warnings. comms should include an example migration guide.
alex: good points. for incompatible param sets when a client pins a model that can't serve them: two options — strict error (400/409) with machine-readable code + suggested fallback, or server-side graceful fallback to compatible model. propose: default -> return machine-readable error and include a `suggested_model` field and an `X-RW-ERROR` header so clients can handle automatically if they want. example:
```http
HTTP/1.1 409 Conflict
X-RW-ERROR: model_param_conflict
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"requested param 'nucleus' not supported by model v1","suggested_model":"v2"}
```
zach: My preference is graceful fallback for user-facing apps, but I agree the error-first approach is safer for strict apps. If we do fallback it must be explicit in the response (model_version) and deterministic. Maybe default to error and provide a config flag `allow_model_fallback` per org.
emily: yes to machine-readable codes. let's standardize error codes like `model_param_conflict`, `model_not_available`, `deprecated_model`. SDKs can map these to exceptions. also include `model_version` in successful responses, e.g.:
```json
{"model_version":"v2","result":{...}}
```
alex: owner questions: who takes docs + SDK updates, who adds telemetry/metrics, who will own the feature-flag rollout?
emily: I can own docs + SDK PRs. will open a draft later today.
zach: I'll wire server-side support + metrics. plan to add a feature flag `accept_model_header` behind FF and default off for 2 weeks. will open PR and tag @emily for SDK examples.
dena: i'll own the deprecation schedule and comms. add me to the RFC and I'll craft the timeline + email templates.
deploy-bot: Reminder: feature-flag rollout template suggests canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 weeks; recommended canary date: 2026-04-01 in us-west.
alex: thanks all — i'll draft the RFC & RFC link (draft): https://redwood.internal/rfcs/123-accept-model-header — will drop tasks there and tag owners (@emily @zach @dena). if no objections by EOD PST i'll ask zach to merge the FF PR to canary. :+1:
